take_homes: you can't share an agent. what travels is context, a skill, output or an interface, and the thing worth sharing is the corrections i made, not the agent file
start from the teammate's job, and ask what would make them drop their current tool for mine. my 'build it for sales over the weekend' habit fails this
an unnamed maintainer or owner in the people plan is the actual finding. a clean technical plan doesn't mean the thing is done

monday.move: don't build the sales setup. ask one sales lead how they do their weekly pipeline prep today and what they'd drop it for. then write down who would maintain whatever I build, or decide not to build it
monday.who: one sales lead, plus our head of revops as possible owner
monday.when: tue or wed, a 20 minute chat
monday.stop_condition: if they say the current spreadsheet is fine and nobody wants to own it, i don't build it
monday.blocker: the weekend urge to just build a bigger version, and nobody outside engineering has asked for this

misconception.why: checking still feels like ceremony for me personally. but the point that the value is in my corrections and judgment on outputs undercuts 'if the agent is good the output is good'. i skipped the review step again anyway, so it only half landed

one_line: the first half is a good brake on building stuff nobody asked for, the lecture drags and has some corporate filler in it. it didn't give me anything on running this across a whole org, but it did make me ask who maintains it.
